tracks.name: Custom Analytics Dashboard for Metis
tracks.description:
Develop a comprehensive analytics dashboard for the Metis L2 blockchain. This platform should provide in-depth insights into network activity, including transaction patterns, contract interactions, cross-layer transactions and network scalability indicators. The dashboards should enhance visibility into network operations, helping developers, researchers and regular users in making informed decisions.
## 🗂️ Bounty Category
  
Launch MVP on Testnet or Mainet
## 📚 Resources
  
https://docs.metis.io/dev/
https://github.com/MetisProtocol/metis-verifier-node
https://docs.ormi.xyz/metis-subgraphs/
https://github.com/vmmunoza/Metis-Analytics-Dashboard

  
https://youtu.be/xcU0c26OYQo
## 🏆 Winner Breakdown
  
1st Place gets $3,500.
## 📝 Requirements
  
Requirements for Completion
- Data Aggregation: Efficiently collect and aggregate Metis on-chain data.
- User Interface: Design an intuitive and navigable interface.
- Data Visualization: Implement interactive and informative data visualizations.
- Accessibility: Ensure the dashboard is accessible and user-friendly.
## ✅ What does a successful project look like?
  
Success Criteria and Features
- Functionality: The dashboard must accurately display real-time and historical data.
- Innovation: Creative features that offer unique insights or perspectives.
- Interactivity: Interactive elements such as clickable charts or customizable views.
- Efficiency: Fast loading times and efficient data processing.
## 🎨 UI/UX Design Requirements
  
UI/UX Design Requirements
- Aesthetics: Clean, professional design aligning with Metis branding.
- Navigation: Intuitive layout and easy navigation.
- Responsiveness: Compatibility with various devices and screen sizes.
## 🤝 Impact on our organization
  
Impact on Metis
- Enhanced Visibility: Providing clear insights into network activities is something that we really look forward to. It will be of significant importance to everyone in our ecosystem.
- Decision Support: This will also help in decision-making processes for developers, researchers and regular users.
## 🧑‍⚖️ How are we judging it?
  
Judging Criteria
- Adherence to Requirements: Fulfillment of the listed tasks and features.
- Innovative Approach: Creativity in addressing the challenge.
- User Experience: Quality of the UI/UX design.
- Technical Execution: Code quality, efficiency, and use of best practices.
- Potential Impact: The perceived value and impact on the Metis ecosystem.
## 👀 Some example projects
  
Use Case Examples
- Transaction Pattern Analysis: A feature allowing users to analyze trends in transaction types over time (e.g., token transfers, contract executions, staking operations).
- Smart Contract Interaction Tracker: A module to monitor and analyze the frequency and types of smart contract interactions.
- Network Health Dashboard: A comprehensive overview of the network's status, including block times, node performance, and transaction throughput.
## 💰 Grant and Investment Opportunities
  
Metis has a grant program called Metis Ecosystem Development Fund (Metis EDF). It is a 4.6 million METIS fund dedicated to accelerating adoption in the Metis ecosystem. The Metis EDF will be used to fund grants for new project deployments, and product development for existing dApps. This grant is also open to support individuals and teams who get involved with us in ETHDenver and want to continue building on Metis.

tracks.name: Metis dApp Analytics Dashboard
tracks.description:
Develop a detailed analytics dashboard tailored for dApps on the Metis blockchain, utilizing the integration with the Allium data platform.
The dashboard should enable users to query, analyze, and visualize key metrics and data related to the performance and usage of dApps on the Metis network.
## 🗂️ Bounty Category
  
Launch MVP on Testnet or Mainet
## 📚 Resources
  
https://docs.allium.so/allium-app/explorer-api/quickstart
https://github.com/vmmunoza/Metis-dApp-Analytics
https://docs.metis.io/dev/

  
https://youtu.be/xcU0c26OYQo
## 🏆 Winner Breakdown
  
1st Place gets $1,000
## 📝 Requirements
  
Requirements for Completion
- Data Integration: Leverage the Metis-Allium integration to access and display relevant data related to Metis dApps.
- Analytics Features: Implement features that provide insights into dApp performance, such as transaction volumes, user interactions, and smart contract events.
- Real-Time Data Processing: Ensure the dashboard can process and display data in real-time or near real-time.
- Customizable Reports: Allow users to create and customize their reports and queries.
## ✅ What does a successful project look like?
  
Success Criteria and Features
- Comprehensive Data Analysis: The dashboard should offer in-depth analysis tools to explore various aspects of dApp performance on Metis.
- User Engagement Tracking: Features to track user engagement and interaction with different dApps.
- Performance Metrics: Tools to measure and display key performance indicators of dApps, like transaction throughput and smart contract execution times.
- Historical Data Analysis: Capability to view and analyze historical data trends.
## 🎨 UI/UX Design Requirements
  
UI/UX Design Requirements
- Intuitive Interface: Easy to navigate and understand, even for users with limited technical expertise.
- Responsive Design: Functional and visually appealing on a variety of devices and screen sizes.
- Visual Aesthetics: A clean and modern design that aligns with Metis’ branding.
## 🤝 Impact on our organization
  
Impact on Metis Ecosystem
- Enhanced dApp Insights: Provides valuable information for dApp developers and users, helping to improve decision-making and strategy.
- Increased Transparency: Offers greater visibility into the activities and performance of dApps on Metis, fostering trust and engagement.
- Community Growth: Encourages more informed and active participation in the Metis ecosystem.
## 🧑‍⚖️ How are we judging it?
  
Judging Criteria
- Functionality and Relevance: Accuracy and relevance of the data provided.
- Innovation and Creativity: Innovative use of data to provide unique insights.
- User Experience: Quality of the UI/UX design, ease of use, and navigation.
- Technical Proficiency: Code efficiency, scalability, and use of best practices.
- Overall Impact: Potential usefulness and impact on the Metis ecosystem.
## 👀 Some example projects
  
Example Use Cases
- dApp Performance Benchmarking: Comparing the transaction throughput, user base growth, and other performance metrics of various dApps.
- User Behavior Insights: Analyzing how users interact with different dApps, such as most active times, transaction sizes, and user demographics.
- Cross-dApp Interaction Analysis: Examine how different dApps on the Metis network interact with each other. Identify trends in cross-dApp transactions, collaborations, or dependencies that could reveal synergies or network effects within the Metis ecosystem.
## 💰 Grant and Investment Opportunities
  
Metis has a grant program called Metis Ecosystem Development Fund (Metis EDF). It is a 4.6 million METIS fund dedicated to accelerating adoption in the Metis ecosystem. The Metis EDF will be used to fund grants for new project deployments, and product development for existing dApps. This grant can also support the builders who decide to participate at ETHDenver and continue to build after the event.

tracks.name: Simplify DeFi with 0x APIs
tracks.description:
Tokenized value is the core of web3. Use 0x APIs to simplify the DeFi experience! Seeking innovative projects that enable seamless access to tokenized value, with a focus on token on/off ramps, gaming and NFT infrastructure, and trading automation.
## 🗂️ Bounty Category
  
Feature Integration
## 📚 Resources
  
- 0x Docs
    - Swap API
    - Tx Relay API
    - Price API
- Github Link
    - 0x demo app examples
- Guides
    - Get started with Swap API
    - Get started with Price API
    - Get started with Tx Relay API
- Videos
    - 0x videos
    - 0x YouTube

  
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NGQcLbeFUKs
## 🏆 Winner Breakdown
  
- 1st place gets $3,000
- 2nd place gets $2,500
- 3rd place gets $1,500
- Seamless UX: $1,000
- Most Innovative: $1,000
- Most Scalable: $1,000
If there are not enough projects to fit all categories, judges may choose to only hand out some of the prizes listed above, or prize amounts may be adjusted, with an explanation provided. 

After the Hackathon…
Prize winners and participants of the 0x bounty may be selected for future collaborations or partnerships. We love featuring our integrators and helping them!
## 📝 Requirements
  
In addition to the judging requirements below, we are seeking projects that align with one of the following categories. These categories are designed to focus your innovation on key areas of the DeFi ecosystem where 0x APIs can have a significant impact:

1. Token On/Off Ramp: Projects should facilitate seamless token deposits, allowing users to use any tokens in their wallet without needing to leave the app to swap for a required token. For example, many apps require ETH, but users do not always have ETH on-hand and need to go to a third-party to make the exchange. By integrating 0x Swap and Tx Relay APIs, users can swap directly in-app into whatever token rather. This could even be automated in the back-end without users needing to take direct action. Focus on streamlining the user experience for entering and exiting token positions.
    a. Examples include but are not limited to Decentralized Indices, Lending, Perps, Derivatives, Yield Farming, Prediction Markets, Liquid Staking, Tokenized RWA, and Insurance Platforms. The sky's the limit!
2. Gaming and NFT Infrastructure: If your project is centered around web3 gaming or NFT infrastructure/marketplace, leverage 0x to enable users to conveniently swap into required tokens directly within your NFT marketplace or in-game environment. Your solution should enhance the user experience in acquiring, trading, or utilizing NFTs.
3. Trading Automation Tools & Infrastructure: Develop tools or infrastructure that automate aspects of trading using 0x APIs. Focus on innovations that enhance trading efficiency, accuracy, and accessibility for users in the DeFi space.
    a. Examples include but are limited to Risk Management tools, Trading bots, Solvers, Decentralized Mutual Funds, DeFi Index Rebalancing, Cross-chain interoperability (Swap API + CCTP)
4. Open Category: If your team has an innovative idea that does not fit into the above categories, we encourage you to discuss it with the 0x team. Visit us at our booth or reach out on the 0x Discord to explore how your unique concept can contribute to the 0x ecosystem.

Engagement with 0x Team: Join the 0x Discord! We highly encourage all participants to engage with the 0x team for guidance, feedback, or to discuss ideas that fall outside the predefined categories. Our team is available to support you throughout the hackathon, ensuring your project aligns well with our vision and APIs.
## ✅ What does a successful project look like?
  
Success in this bounty hinges not only on technical proficiency but also on creativity, usability, and real-world applicability. Here are key features that would indicate a successful implementation, along with examples to guide builders:

1. Seamless 0x API Integration: A successful project integrate at least one of 0x APIs (Swap, Tx Relay, Price) in a way that feels natural and enhances the core functionality. For example, a token on/off ramp that uses the Swap API to allow users to effortlessly convert tokens within the app, reducing the need for external exchanges.
2. User-Centric Design: The project should prioritize the user experience, making complex DeFi interactions intuitive. For instance, a trading automation tool that offers a user-friendly interface for setting up and managing automated trades, catering to both novice and experienced traders.
3. Innovative Use Cases: We're looking for projects that push the boundaries of what's possible with 0x APIs. An example might be a gaming platform where in-game assets (NFTs) can be directly traded or swapped using 0x, seamlessly integrating with the game's economy.
4. Scalability and Performance: A successful project should not only work well at a small scale but also demonstrate potential for growth. For instance, a marketplace using 0x that significantly simplifies the NFT purchase process, attracting more users to the space due to its ease of use.
5. Documentation and Presentation: Comprehensive documentation and a clear, compelling presentation of the project are essential. This includes both the technical implementation as well as explanations of the design choices and how the project addresses specific user needs or market gaps.

Example of a Successful Feature Implementation:
Consider a gaming project in the Token On/Off Ramp category that enables users to deposit an array of ERC-20 tokens and automatically swaps them into the required token (e.g., ETH or a game-specific token) without leaving the platform. This project would demonstrate success through its seamless integration of the Swap API, providing a frictionless experience for users, enhancing liquidity, and demonstrating a clear understanding of user needs in the DeFi space.
## 🎨 UI/UX Design Requirements
  
If the project is user-facing, the following UI/UX requirements will be considered: 
1. Intuitiveness and Simplicity: The interface should be intuitive, even for users who are new to DeFi. Avoid overcomplicating the design. Simplify navigation and make key functionalities easily accessible.
2. Consistency and Clarity: Maintain a consistent design language throughout the application. Use clear, concise language and familiar icons to ensure that the functionality is easily understood.
3. User-Centric Approach: Design with the end-user in mind. This includes understanding the user journey, anticipating user needs, and designing to solve user problems effectively.
## 🤝 Impact on our organization
  
1. Feedback and Improvement: Working with external teams provides valuable feedback on the 0x APIs and infrastructure. This feedback is crucial for continuous improvement and can guide future development and enhancements.
2. Ecosystem Growth: 0x APIs are built on the open-sourced 0x Protocol. As teams work on projects integrating 0x APIs, they contribute to the growth and robustness of the 0x ecosystem which support the broader flow of tokenized value across the ecosystem to all contributors. 
3. Marketing Collaborations: Participants of the 0x bounty may be selected for future collaborations or partnerships. We love featuring our integrators and helping them!
## 🧑‍⚖️ How are we judging it?
  
All submissions must fulfill the following requirements to be considered valid:
1. 🛠 Implement at least one 0x APIs - Swap, Tx Relay, Price
    a. Created a 0x Dashboard account to obtain a 0x API key (test key is okay)
    b. Properly calls one of the API endpoints (e.g. Swap API /quote endpoint, Tx Relay /submit endpoint, Price /quote endpoint)
    c. The use case for the endpoint(s) makes sense from a user perspective
2. 💻 Technical Implementation
    a. The code well-written, technically sound, and clean
    b. Projects that are code-complete will have higher consideration than projects that are just in ideation
3. ✨ Innovation & Creativity
    a. The solution should not only be functional but also innovative. We are looking for unique approaches that stand out in terms of design, usability, or technical implementation.
4. 🌈 Design
    a. If the project is user-facing, project should demonstrate a clear understanding of user needs and present an interface that is intuitive and accessible.
5. 🌐 Adoption & Market
    a. The project has potential to gain real-world traction
    b. The project fills a market gap and has the potential to be adopted by a sizable and diverse audience
6. Project Scope & Overall Presentation
    a. Project scope is clearly defined and conveys how the solution simplifies or enhances the DeFi experience
    b. Project clearly describes the app architecture, codebase, and how the 0x APIs are integrated and utilized.
## 👀 Some example projects
  
Please see the "What is required to complete this prize?" section for full details of each category. We are seeking projects that align with one of the following categories: 
1. Token On/Off Ramp
    a. Examples include but are not limited to Decentralized Indices, Lending, Perps, Derivatives, Yield Farming, Prediction Markets, Liquid Staking, Tokenized RWA, and Insurance Platforms. The sky's the limit!
2. Gaming and NFT Infrastructure
    a. If your project is centered around web3 gaming or NFT infrastructure/marketplace, leverage 0x to enable users to conveniently swap into required tokens directly within your NFT marketplace or in-game environment. Your solution should enhance the user experience in acquiring, trading, or utilizing NFTs.
3. Trading Automation Tools & Infrastructure
    a. Examples include but are limited to Risk Management tools, Trading bots, Solvers, Decentralized Mutual Funds, DeFi Index Rebalancing, Cross-chain interoperability (Swap API + CCTP)
4. Open Category
    a. If your team has an innovative idea that does not fit into the above categories, we encourage you to discuss it with the 0x team. Visit us at our booth or reach out on the 0x Discord to explore how your unique concept can contribute to the 0x ecosystem.
## 💼 Job Opportunities
  
Find open 0x positions at: https://0x.org/careers

tracks.name: ZetaChain Best Omnichain Contract
tracks.description:
Create a unique and advanced decentralized application (dapp) using ZetaChain's advanced omnichain contracts that works with the world's top cryptocurrency, Bitcoin. By using this state-of-the-art technology, your dapp will be able to provide secure and smooth transactions, improve user experiences, and change the way users interact with blockchains. Make the most of ZetaChain's power and create an outstanding dapp that will make a lasting impact on the industry.
## 🗂️ Bounty Category
  
Launch MVP on Testnet or Mainet
## 📚 Resources
  
- Explore the Omnichain contracts overview and check out the helpful tutorials. You can also watch the informative Omnichain swap tutorial (video) for inspiration.
- Check out the Omnichain staking tutorial (compatible with Bitcoin), the Omnichain swap tutorial (compatible with Bitcoin), and the Bitcoin frontend tutorial for valuable insights and guidance.

  
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0Mlfvtc4wR4
## 🏆 Winner Breakdown
  
We're excited to award the top two team projects the following prizes
- 1st place can get as much as $5,000.
- 2nd place will get at least $1,000.

If we get less than two projects, or they're not meeting our criteria, the prize money might change. The range for the total awarded prize in this bounty could be anywhere between $2,000 and $10,000. Also, if no project meets our criteria enough to win, we'll explain why
## 📝 Requirements
  
Develop a decentralized application (dapp) that leverages ZetaChain's omnichain contracts capabilities, ensuring compatibility with Ethereum, Polygon, BSC, and Bitcoin. The dapp should offer practical utility for users of connected blockchains, Bitcoin and ZetaChain while providing an user-friendly interface for seamless interaction. The dapp should also implement custom logic that demonstrates innovation and uniqueness, rather than relying on tutorials or simple examples.
## ✅ What does a successful project look like?
  
A decentralized application that utilizes ZetaChain's interoperability features, offers practical utility for users of connected blockchains, Bitcoin and ZetaChain while providing a convenient interface for interacting with the dapp.
## 🎨 UI/UX Design Requirements
  
The UI/UX design of the decentralized application should prioritize a user-friendly interface that enhances the overall user experience. It should be intuitive, visually appealing, and easy to navigate. Consider implementing clear visual cues, concise and informative messaging, and smooth interactions to ensure a seamless and enjoyable user journey.
## 🤝 Impact on our organization
  
A team working on this bounty would have a significant impact on our ecosystem. They would demonstrate the capabilities of ZetaChain's advanced technologies and showcase the potential for innovation in the industry. By creating unique and advanced decentralized applications (dapps) using ZetaChain's omnichain contracts, the team would contribute to the growth and adoption of ZetaChain, attracting more users and developers to the platform.
## 🧑‍⚖️ How are we judging it?
  
- Implement the onCrossChainCall functionality to enable seamless interaction with different chains and Bitcoin.
- Ensure compatibility with Bitcoin, and consider additional compatibility with Ethereum, Polygon, and BSC.
- Utilize ZRC-20 tokens to enhance the contract's capabilities and efficient asset management.
- Implement custom logic that demonstrates innovation and uniqueness (not tutorials or simple examples).
## 👀 Some example projects
  
- Omnichain lending protocol to support any native collateral and assets including lending/borrowing native Bitcoin.
- DeFi trading and finance such as omnichain DEXs and other DeFi primitives (AMM, stable swap, orderbook, perps, etc.) incorporating native Bitcoin.
- Omnichain NFT projects or marketplaces that allow users to easily trade and transact with NFTs across chains, take native Bitcoin payments, or leveraging Bitcoin in some way.
- NFTs that are minted or modified from Bitcoin inputs.
- Universal GameFi digital assets platform that abstracts from users the underlying blockchains while enabling Bitcoin for payments or other use cases.
- Governance and DAO tooling that enable groups to span, operate across, or manage assets on multiple chains while letting groups manage, trade or even vote with Bitcoin.
- Web3 social network applications that lower the barrier to entry allowing users from many chains to join while incorporating Bitcoin.
- Universal on-chain identity, accounts, and/or wallets to simplify crypto usage across chains or let users manage Bitcoin holdings in a simple way.
- Any-to-any payments that bring Bitcoin into the broader DeFi ecosystem, unlock Bitcoin for existing applications or allows users/ customers to send from and receive any asset on any chain.
- Ultimate decentralized yield aggregator to monitor and manage digital assets across any DeFi on any chains in one place.
## 💼 Job Opportunities
  
https://www.zetachain.com/careers
## 💰 Grant and Investment Opportunities
  
Gain exposure to VCs in the blockchain industry and ZetaChain ecosystem partners. The winners of the hackathon will be shortlisted for Grant Committee consideration as part of the $5,000,000 [ZetaChain Grants Program](https://www.zetachain.com/grants). Please note that grants awarded may vary based on bespoke agreements.

Grant Program Requirements:
- Deploy a smart contract on ZetaChain’s Testnet and Mainnet’s zEVM and/or leveraging ZetaChain’s omnichain messaging. Learn [how to build your first zEVM smart contract](https://www.zetachain.com/docs/developers/omnichain/tutorials/hello/). All relevant contract deployment addresses should be published publicly. All code for these smart contracts should be open-sourced.
- Both existing projects that want to leverage or migrate to ZetaChain and novel projects in the ideation or development stage are eligible.
- Grant applicants must be legal entities or individuals and agree to ZetaChain’s [Terms of Use](https://www.zetachain.com/terms-of-use).
- Grant should be used to help with web3 development, liquidity, adoption, and/or awareness.
- Grant applicants with strong technical capabilities, and ideally a clear idea of product-market fit and go-to-market as well as ambitious user growth goals will be prioritized.
- Grant applicants must demonstrate a clear use of funds: how a grant will be used to create the proposed application. Clear mission and vision statement and plans for product development is highly encouraged.

tracks.description:
Unlock the full potential of ZetaChain's Cross-Chain Messaging (CCM) capabilities by developing an original and impactful use case. Your project should demonstrate the innovative application of ZetaChain’s CCM between connected EVM chains such as Ethereum, Polygon, and BSC.
## 🗂️ Bounty Category
  
Launch MVP on Testnet or Mainet
## 📚 Resources
  
Explore the Cross-chain messaging overview and get started with the Introductory tutorial to unlock the full potential of cross-chain messaging.

  
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0Mlfvtc4wR4
## 🏆 Winner Breakdown
  
We're excited to award the top two team projects the following prizes:
1st place can get as much as $5,000.
2nd place will get at least $1,000.
If we get less than two projects, or they're not meeting our criteria, the prize money might change. The range for the total awarded prize in this bounty could be anywhere between $2,000 and $10,000. Also, if no project meets our criteria enough to win, we'll explain why
## 📝 Requirements
  
Develop a decentralized application (dapp) that fully leverages the power of ZetaChain's CCM. Your dapp should incorporate the Connector API for messaging across various chains and effectively use the onZetaMessage and onZetaRevert functions to manage and process messages. The dapp must be compatible with all connected chains, including Ethereum, Polygon, and BSC. Ensure that your solution is deployed on ZetaChain's testnet for evaluation.
## ✅ What does a successful project look like?
  
A successful dapp will be one that creatively utilizes ZetaChain’s CCM to provide a new or enhanced utility, demonstrating the power and flexibility of cross-chain messaging.
## 🎨 UI/UX Design Requirements
  
Design a user-friendly, intuitive, and visually appealing interface for your dapp. The UI/UX should facilitate easy navigation and smooth interactions, incorporating clear visual cues and concise messaging. The design should cater to the needs of the users, providing a seamless experience across different blockchain platforms.
## 🤝 Impact on our organization
  
Teams undertaking this challenge will play a pivotal role in showcasing the versatility and power of ZetaChain's cross-chain messaging capabilities. Their innovative solutions will not only demonstrate the practical applications of CCM but also encourage wider adoption and development within the ZetaChain ecosystem, propelling the platform towards becoming a hub for cross-chain communication and transactions.
## 🧑‍⚖️ How are we judging it?
  
- Utilize ZetaChain's Connector API to send messages across different chains.
- Implement the onZetaMessage and onZetaRevert functions to handle and process the received messages effectively.
- Ensure compatibility with all connected chains, including Ethereum, Polygon, and BSC.
- Deploy your solution to ZetaChain's testnet environment for evaluation.
- Implement custom logic that showcases innovation and demonstrates the power of cross-chain messaging (not tutorials or simple examples).
## 👀 Some example projects
  
- Decentralized Exchanges (DEXs): Build next-generation DEXs that enable seamless trading of assets across multiple chains.
- Lending and Borrowing: Create lending platforms that allow users to access credit from different blockchains.
- Financial Instruments: Develop innovative financial instruments like derivatives, stablecoins, and insurance products that work across multiple chains.
- Financial Inclusion: Develop new and more accessible financial tools that can be made even more available to peoples by leveraging omnichain technology.
- Collectibles and Collections: Create unique NFTs and collections that can be accessed and utilized across multiple chains.
- Omnichain DAO Tooling: Build tools and platforms that facilitate cross-chain governance and asset custody.
## 💼 Job Opportunities

tracks.name: IBC Everywhere - Using Union infra to connect Ethereum and Cosmos
tracks.description:
Write a cross-chain dAPP that uses IBC as its underlying message passing layer. Whether this is NFTs, DeFi, or any other arbitrary protocol - the choice is yours. Be creative! 
Use cosmwasm on Union (Testnet) and solidity on EVM (Sepolia Testnet).
## 🗂️ Bounty Category
  
Feature Integration
## 📚 Resources
  
Union explorer: https://testnet.bonlulu.uno/union

Union docs: https://union.build/docs/
- Specifically the pingpong example: https://union.build/docs/demos/pingpong/

IBC docs: https://github.com/cosmos/ibc
Specifically the channel spec: https://github.com/cosmos/ibc/tree/main/spec/core/ics-004-channel-and-packet-semantics

  
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C1FHgGNOPgU
## 🏆 Winner Breakdown
  
First Place gets $1,500
Second Place gets $1,000
## 📝 Requirements
  
Introduction: 
Union has built a sovereign interoperability layer in testnet connecting IBC to Ethereum (Sepolia). The Union network is a hyper-efficient zero-knowledge infrastructure layer for general message passing, asset transfers, NFTs, and DeFi. It’s based on consensus verification and has no dependencies on trusted third parties, oracles, multi-signatures, or MPC.

Background: 
For those who care about decentralization and reliability, and believe that finance should be accessible for everyone. To achieve this, Union has created a truly decentralized interoperability layer that can be bootstrapped by individuals with minimum hardware requirements. 

Scope of Work: 
Your dAPP will require two complimentary smart contracts and access to Union Testnet relayer. The existing light clients will support your work. 
1. Write a smart contract in cosmwasm and upload to the operating Union Testnet. 
2. Write a complimentary smart contract in solidity and deploy on Sepolia.
3. Open a channel between your two smart contracts. 
4. Create a MVP User Interface to interact with your protocol. 
An example of this integration can be found in Union Docs.
## ✅ What does a successful project look like?
  
1. UI will be aesthetically pleasing and intuitive 
2. User’s interactions with Union and Seoplia will be verifiable on chain 
3. All transactions will be linked to a block explorer 
4. Cross-chain functionality should not be part of the UI. The UI will show Union and Sepolia as arbitrary ends of your protocol. Use IBC functionality and the Union SDK.  Metamask wallet integration with leap for cosmos (Union)  is required. The wallet integration is provided by the SDK.
## 🎨 UI/UX Design Requirements
  
1. Integrate your UI with metamask via Union’s SDK 
2. Status updates to show how your protocol is performing, any tx in progress, pending, completed, etc. 
3. Gracefully handle and Errors, and error codes should be human readable. 
4. Links to block explorers 
5. Adaptable UI to a Mobile screen (SDK will not work on mobile but should present on mobile) *Note Metamask mobile browser does not yet support Snaps 
6. Bonus points for light/dark mode
## 🤝 Impact on our organization
  
1. Introduces IBC to the Ethereum community thereby highlighting the usefulness of Union. 
2. Opens the door to solve undiscovered use cases and issues to the Ethereum and Cosmos community.
## 🧑‍⚖️ How are we judging it?
  
1. Operational UI 
2. Correct integrations with Union and Sepolia
3. Secure protocol - ie. no minting arbitrary assets
4. Smart contracts should have feature parity
## 👀 Some example projects
  
Undiscovered use cases - Union wants to learn from the community what they want to solve.
## 💼 Job Opportunities
  
No public information at this time. Hiring may resume later in the year.

tracks.name: Zircuit Analytics Infrastructure
tracks.description:
Build some on- or off-chain analytics for the traffic on Zircuit. It can involve the bridge, gas spendings, active nodes on the network, deployed smart contracts, or anything else. Bring your best data science to visualize the Zircuit ecosystem.
## 🗂️ Bounty Category
  
Feature Integration
## 📚 Resources
  
- Deploy on Zircuit Quick Start https://docs.zircuit.com/build-on-zircuit/deploy-on-zircuit 
- Zircuit RPC Endpoints https://docs.zircuit.com/dev-tools/rpc-endpoints 
- Verifying Contracts on Zircuit https://docs.zircuit.com/dev-tools/verifying-contracts 
- List of Sepolia Faucets https://docs.zircuit.com/dev-tools/faucet 
- Zircuit Discord: https://discord.com/invite/zircuit

  
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=L2iAvngboGQ
## 🏆 Winner Breakdown
  
First place: $2,500
Second place: $1,500
## 📝 Requirements
  
Project smart contracts must be deployed on the Zircuit Testnet and verified via the Zircuit Explorer.

A GitHub repository containing the project artifacts (smart contracts, tests, documentation) and a solid README of the project must be submitted.
The README should include:
- a clear short one-sentence description of your submission
- a short description of what you integrated Zircuit with and how
- short description of the team and their backgrounds
- clear instructions for testing the integration
- feedback describing your experience with building on Zircuit
- optionally, a short video demo or slide deck. 

Any project is eligible as long as these requirements are met. This bounty will select the top three projects deployed on Zircuit.
## ✅ What does a successful project look like?
  
Success looks like a good data visualization tool or system to analyze Zircuit transactions, the network use, or integrations, or something related. The project should be easy to use and clean, and may be inspired by other analytics tools for blockchains. 

A successful submission will include a functional prototype that solves the problem it’s intended to address. It will showcase some innovation and creativity, either through technological or UI improvements. It may be complete and solve a long-standing open problem or introduce something with a lot of potential for future development. Either way, it has an impact on the Zircuit ecosystem.
## 🎨 UI/UX Design Requirements
  
There are no external UI/UX design requirements, though the best projects will be accompanied by a clean interface (or necessary documents). The simple and clear UI can be web-based, through another smart contract integration, or via the command line. Users should be able to interact with Zircuit deployed code via MetaMask connected to the network if applicable. The application (or its documentation) should be responsive and easy to navigate.

Winning projects should have a user-centered design that makes it easy for the target audience. This can be end users or developers integrating the project into their own codebase. The best-of-the-best may also include clean and consistent visual designs.
## 🤝 Impact on our organization
  
These bounties aim to help gain insights into Zircuit network and build the Zircuit ecosystem. In turn, these insights might inspire others to use Zircuit or integrate their own tool into the ecosystem.
## 🧑‍⚖️ How are we judging it?
  
This bounty will be judged based on completeness, usefulness, execution, and creativity.

Completeness and execution mean that the project is functional. These are the most important categories. Winning submissions should be as close to functional as possible and engineered properly. Ideally there are good test cases, designs for complicated use cases, and other supporting documentation. The sophistication of the code and whether it implements the project requirements may be considered. However, a brilliant but incomplete dApp is less impressive than one that works completely. 

Usefulness means the benefit that it brings to the users and overall Zircuit community. Try to come up with a hack that is not useful and interesting just to you, but also to the others.

Creativity is paramount on this bounty. Winning projects should motivate their decision to build this solution, indicating which new problem they are solving, how they are solving a problem differently, or what new technology they are bringing to Zircuit.
## 👀 Some example projects
  
Some examples might include Dune dashboards, custom NFT trackers, or tools to track proof generation time. You could integrate data into Discord or Slack, or present it on a website.
## 💼 Job Opportunities
  
Zircuit is always looking for the best and brightest team members to build the best possible rollup. If you submit a project to this bounty and are looking for blockchain development (Solidity, Go, Rust) or cryptographer roles, please email jan@zircuit.com with the header [ETHDenver Job Hunter].

tracks.description:
Create a solution that abstracts away the complexities of blockchain networks, enabling seamless interaction and transactions for users across multiple chains within a single interface. The goal is to enhance the user experience and facilitate mainstream adoption of decentralized applications. 
You can build a feature for your pre-existing project or code something from scratch.
## 🗂️ Bounty Category
  
Feature Integration
## 📚 Resources
  
Basic dev resources: https://linktr.ee/neardevhub
NEARs Account Model:

- Deploying Contracts and SubAccounts https://docs.near.org/sdk/rust/promises/deploy-contract 
- Create A Sub Account from NEAR Cli https://docs.near.org/tutorials/crosswords/basics/add-functions-call#create-a-subaccount 
- Delegate Action https://nomicon.io/RuntimeSpec/Actions#delegate-actions
- What is an Implicit Account https://docs.near.org/integrator/implicit-accounts#:~:text=Implicit%20accounts%20work%20similarly%20to,representation%20of%20the%20public%20key. 
- NEAR’s Account Model by Mike Purvis pt1 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ganXZ0Iw1C8 pt2 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4Q4K03t2P48 
- NEAR Account https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dgu4FT1Bt3o 
- NEAR CROSSWORD walkthrough https://youtu.be/HNPkod4sTyQ?si=GOYwhXIoyvsmAvDq 
- NEAR Names https://github.com/near-examples/nearnames 
- Storage Staking https://docs.near.org/concepts/storage/storage-staking 
Locked Accounts https://docs.near.org/concepts/basics/accounts/access-keys#locked-accounts
## 🏆 Winner Breakdown
  
We're giving money prizes to up to three team projects:
3rd place will get at least $1,000.
1st place can get as much as $10,000.
If we get less than three projects, or they're not meeting our criteria, the prize money might change.
## 📝 Requirements
  
Must have:
- Develop a user-friendly interface that allows users to transact, interact with dapps, and manage assets across different blockchain networks effortlessly (make sure to include Near :).
- Implement account abstraction functionality, enabling users to use a single account for interacting with dapps on various chains.
- Ensure interoperability between different chains, allowing assets to be transferred seamlessly without the need for users to understand the underlying blockchain technology.
- Provide secure and private transactions for users, with built-in features to handle gas fees, network switching, and other complexities seamlessly yet transparently
Bonus points:
- Integration with popular dapps or protocols such as Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, etc., to demonstrate interoperability and functionality across multiple chains.

## 🎨 UI/UX Design Requirements
  
Must have a functional browser-based or mobile interface, not a Figma demo.
## 🤝 Impact on our organization
  
Please ensure that your submission aligns with the principles of chain abstraction outlined in Illia Polosukhin's blog post and contributes to the goal of advancing mainstream adoption of Web3 through improved usability and interoperability.
## 🧑‍⚖️ How are we judging it?
  
- User Experience: How intuitive and seamless is the interface for users to interact with dapps and manage assets across chains?
- Functionality: Does the solution effectively abstract away the complexities of blockchain networks while providing robust interoperability and security features?
- Innovation: Does the project incorporate novel approaches or technologies to improve the user experience and advance the vision of chain abstraction in Web3?
- Bonus points for documentation: Is there clear documentation provided to guide developers and users on using the platform and understanding its capabilities?
## 👀 Some example projects
  
Here are some ideas from Near and Near adjacent project teams: https://banyan-collective.notion.site/Ideas-Abstraction-2834780030d74af0ae0779e32baacff4

tracks.description:
Although Polkadot is a network of interoperable layer-1 chains, users really shouldn’t even know what chain they're using when interacting with Polkadot. What should matter is what they intend to achieve. This bounty seeks dApp submissions that push this narrative.
## 🗂️ Bounty Category
  
Launch MVP on Testnet or Mainet
## 📚 Resources
  
Highlevel
- What is Polkadot? - A Short Introduction (video)
- Build dApps with Substrate Connect (video)
- Learn about Polkadot appchains (aka "parachains") (wiki)

Start coding
- Polkadot Cloud: a library and platform for developing and publishing assets for Polkadot dApps.
- Polkadot JS API: the Javascript library for interacting with Substrate blockchains
- Subxt / Yew UI integration: an example of building a UI entirely in Rust 
- Substrate Connect: Run Wasm Light Clients of any Substrate based chain directly in your browser
- Sidecar: REST service that makes it easy to interact with blockchain nodes built using Substrate

  
https://youtu.be/JKlXjTw6TY0

- Code submission: A repository with a hosted demo URL of the webapp and instructions on how to run it locally 
- README file: A description of the user journey with screenshots and needs your app serves and how you plan to extend it
- Demo: Short 2-minute video showing how to interact with your UI
- Bonus: Make your application mobile friendly
- Bonus: Make your application light client compatible
## ✅ What does a successful project look like?
  
Successful submissions will serve an actual need in the ecosystem or provide a fun, different way to do things on Polkadot that doesn't already exist.

This bounty is ideally looking for submissions that create a UI that allows users to interact with the core Polkadot system (i.e. the relay chain and its system chains). Currently there’s the AssetHub, Bridgehub and Collectives live on mainnet. There are others on Kusama (Encointer) and Rococo (Peoples) too. You may chose which network you want to build a UI for. Submissions will be judged on the usefulness and user experience of your application.
## 🎨 UI/UX Design Requirements
  
Your dapp must be published to a publicly accessible demo URL.
## 🤝 Impact on our organization

- Usefulness and uniqueness: does your hack address a need? What sets you apart from other projects doing similar things? How does your submission benefit Polkadot?

- Viewing the activity and engaging as members of on-chain collectives (see: UX guidelines for the Polkadot Fellowship)

Support from Square One (Substrate Builder's Program) and W3F grants.

tracks.description:
The Polkadot SDK -- used by to build over 50 layer-1 chains secured by Polkadot as well as other projects outside of Polkadot such as Madara (Starknet), Midnight (Cardano) and Polygon Avail -- is a powerful open source SDK that allows teams to build custom blockchains. Launch MVP on Testnet or Mainet

Highlevel

- Demo: Short 2-minute video showing your local testnet up and running

- Bonus: teams who demonstrate the use of XCM and use more than one appchain in their demo
## ✅ What does a successful project look like?
  
We're looking for a working proof of concept appchain that could become deployed to Polkadot. Successful submissions are ones that:
- Provide a unique service to the Polkadot network and its existing appchains
- Identify and meet a need for Polkadot's end-users and ecosystem agents

Teams will have integrated their custom appchain pallets into a parachain template and will provide a clear demonstration of its use as a POC and plans for future development. This bounty seeks submissions of proof of concepts with a clear idea for an appchain that can benefit the Polkadot ecosystem. These may get your creative juices flowing:
- Recreate the logic of a popular L1 or L2 in another ecosystem
- Implement the logic of an existing dApp as it’s own appchain
- Extend the core logic of an existing system chain

Support from Square One and W3F grants.

tracks.name: Build an App to Track & Reward the Activities of the Ambassadors of the Filecoin Orbit Program
tracks.description:
Build an app on Filecoin & Filecoin Virtual Machine that tracks Filecoin Orbit Volunteer Ambassador activities and provides rewards in the form of NFT “achievements” and associated ERC20 token reward points.
## 🗂️ Bounty Category
  
Launch MVP on Testnet or Mainet
## 📚 Resources
  
- FVM Docs: https://docs.filecoin.io/smart-contracts/fundamentals/the-fvm
- Filecoin docs: https://docs.filecoin.io/ 
- FVM Hackathon Cheatsheet: https://github.com/filecoin-project/community/discussions/585

  
https://youtu.be/Na_YuIC7r4Q
## 🏆 Winner Breakdown
  
We are giving money prizes to the top three team projects: 
The 1st place grand prize winning project team will win at minimum $5,000, at most $7,500.  
Two runner-up prize winning project teams will win at minimum $1,000, at most $2,500 each.

If we get less than three projects, or they're not meeting our criteria, the prize money might change.  If no project meets our criteria enough to win, we'll explain why.
## 📝 Requirements
  
The Bounty
The 1st prize bounty of $5,000 - $7,500 will be awarded to one team of hackers that builds an app on Filecoin & Filecoin Virtual Machine that tracks Orbit member activities and provides rewards in the form of NFT “achievements” and associated ERC20 token reward points. Two runner-up prizes for high quality projects that come close to winning will be offered, each in the amount of $1,000 - $2,500. A total of $9,500 will be rewarded.

Each achievement should be an ERC721 token, and associated reward points should be ERC20 tokens. Although these latter ERC20 tokens are spendable and can be redeemed for rewards, the app should track lifetime points earned regardless of if they are spent, and present this number to the Ambassador as their “score.”  

Requirements
The app should be a simple web dashboard that has a number of pages, with some permissioned actions available only to certain profile types.  The pages, and their features, should include, but are not limited to, the following:  

- A sign in page, where Orbit Ambassadors sign in with Metamask / Filecoin address.  There should be be three account types: 
    - Standard Orbit Ambassadors.  Orbit Ambassadors are volunteers who engage in various activities in the Filecoin ecosystem.
    - Orbit Regional Leads, who will have certain special privileges.  Regional leads are volunteers who provide guidance to Orbit Ambassadors and set the strategy for Orbit activities in a continent wide region.
    - Filecoin Foundation staff, which will allow the staff to approve an achievement before it is issued to an Orbit member.
- An activities page, which will: 
    - For the Orbit Ambassador, the activities page should show them an aggregate summary of their past activities. 
    - For Regional Leads, the activities section should have a drop down with a list of all Ambassadors in their region, showing the same page a selected Orbit Ambassador would see.
    - For Filecoin Foundation staff, a summary with visualizations of global activities.
- An Achievements page, which should include: 
    - For the Orbit Ambassador, a list of all achievements, clearly showing which ones they have earned, followed by which they are close to earning, followed by all others they have not yet earned. 
    - For the regional lead, a chronological notifications page showing recent achievements earned by Ambassadors in their region.  
    - For the Filecoin Foundation Staff, proposed achievements for Orbit Ambassadors pending approval by that Staff member. 
- A rewards section, where: 
    - Orbit Ambassadors can see a list of rewards and their associated needed points, and redeem.  
    - Regional Leads can see which rewards were redeemed by their Orbit Ambassadors. 
    - Filecoin Foundation staff can add a reward and set the number of points needed to redeem.  
- Leaderboard
    - The app should generate a public-facing leaderboard showing which Orbit Ambassadors have the highest number of earned ERC20 points.   
- A profile page, where users can set privacy permissions. 

Additional requirement include: 
- The app must use a Filecoin address as a sign-in for each Orbit Ambassador.  Filecoin Foundation staff must sign-in with a fil.org email address.  
- The app must include smart deployments on Filecoin Virtual Machine.  This may be limited to simply the ERC721 and ERC20 tokens needed for issuing achievements, or it may include more involved governance logic.  
- The app must be able to seamlessly pull and present data from AirTable. 
- The app’s leaderboard must be able to be embedded on external websites.
- The Orbit Ambassador profile page must include an opt-out or “show anonymously” option from the public leaderboard.
## ✅ What does a successful project look like?
  
A successful app will track data on Orbit member activities and clearly display all relevant information on the site.  

Events Tracker 
Orbit members spend most of their time hosting academic workshops or community hackathons locally.  

The Orbit program currently tracks Orbit activities by having members report their activities through AirTable forms, which generates a database of this data.   The database includes a range of data, including: 

- Number of events hosted. 
- Number of attendees for each event.
- Event Costs.
- Event location. 
- Standardized event content. 

The Orbit app should associate this data with each signed-in Orbit Ambassador, and automatically propose to the Filecoin Foundation staff achievements based on the Orbit member’s accomplishments.  For an idea of what event achievements could be, a short list of achievements can be found HERE.  

Social Media Data Collection & Tracker
One of the largest challenges the Orbit program has is in tracking social media data.  Orbit Ambassadors engage with their communities through a range of social media platforms, and we’d like to track that data and issue appropriate “achievements.” 

The following are social media platforms most used by Orbit Ambassadors and potential data points to track:   

- Twitter, including number of tweets, their impression, likes, and retweets. 
- Medium, including number of articles posted and each of their “claps.”
- YouTube, including number of videos posted, number of likes, and number of comments. 
- Mentions in traditional press. 
- Telegram or WhatsApp, including the number of people in their community group chat. 
- Slack or Discord messages, specifically, replies by Orbit members in specific channels.

Each one of these platforms has an API that allows a third party app to pull data from the platform.  The Orbit app should do the following: 
- Use APIs to pull in the relevant data from the social media platform.  
- Associate one social media account from each platform with the Orbit Ambassador’s MetaMask/Filecoin Address sign in to the Orbit app. 
- The app should automatically propose achievements based on social media account activity.   For an idea of what the social media achievements will be, a short list of achievements can be found HERE.  
- Present the social media data for each Orbit Ambassador to Filecoin Foundation staff accounts.  Note that the Filecoin Foundation uses AirTable as its database platform of choice.

Hackathons Tracker
One of the goals of the Orbit program is to encourage Orbit community members to attend and submit at hackathons.  The Orbit app should track, for each Orbit Ambassador, the full list of all GitHub accounts from attendees of events that Ambassador has hosted.  This data is available on AirTable. 

A page available to the Filecoin Foundation staff should then be able to upload a list of GitHub accounts that have submitted a project at a hackathon, along with whether that GitHub account won a prize.   The Orbit app would then cross reference the lists of GitHub accounts associated with each Orbit Ambassador, and issue relevant achievements if a community member of theirs submitted at / won a given hackathon.
## 🎨 UI/UX Design Requirements
  
In addition to the requirements above, here are some additional comments on our UI/UX expectations: 

- Design | The app’s design and visualizations should be clear and easily understood by non-engineers.  Consideration should be given to page colors and fonts –the Filecoin Foundation design standards can be found here.  Projects that demonstrate consideration as to which data was best to wrangle and which charts and visualizations are most  compelling and understandable will score higher.   

- User Experience | The app’s user interface should be simple to use and make every attempt to reduce the number of manual steps needed to perform any given action.  As an example, let’s look at the action of “the Filecoin Foundation staffer approves an automatically proposed achievement for an Orbit Ambassador.”   One way to design this functionality would be for the Filecoin Foundation staff page to show a drop down list of all Orbit Ambassadors, and then show proposed achievements on a separate page for any given Orbit Ambassador, with each achievement having a button for approval.  An alternative design would be to have one page with a chronological list of the most recent automatically proposed achievements, with a button for approval for each achievement listed.  The latter design would score higher because the former design required three mouse clicks and two pages to complete the task of approving the achievement, while the latter design requires only one mouse click and one page.
## 🤝 Impact on our organization
  
The Filecoin Orbit Community program is Filecoin Foundation's developer community and education program, where 150+ volunteer Orbit Ambassadors in 80+ countries host Filecoin workshops and hackathons, publish Filecoin educational materials, build software projects on Filecoin, and much more.   You can learn more about the Filecoin Orbit program at orbitcommunity.filecoin.io. 

This app will help us recognize and reward the great work of our Orbit Ambassadors, elevating our program and making it easier to get involved as an Ambassador.
## 🧑‍⚖️ How are we judging it?
  
Protocol Labs and Filecoin Foundation score on five categories.  In addition to the design requirements listed above, here are two additional categories worth commenting on: 

- Technological Progress | Naturally, the Filecoin Foundation would like to see the Orbit app built on Filecoin Virtual Machine with Orbit Ambassador accounts being linked to their Filecoin Address on Metamask.  A critical component of the app will be the ERC721 and ERC20 tokens deployed on Filecoin Virtual Machine.  Projects that seamlessly integrate Filecoin into the app will be scored highest –examples include both making the Filecoin backend un-noticeable to the user (for example, all rewards points are ERC20 tokens but on the app, the user only sees  a “points” total ) AND making it easy for users to see their activity on a block explorer by providing links (for example, a link to a block explorer to a user’s wallet where their NFT achievement would be shown).   Unique uses of Filecoin’s inherent features would also be looked upon favorably –for example, a leaderboard can be generated from the data on AirTable, OR a leaderboard can be generated from the public facing ERC20 tokens associated with each of the Orbit Ambassadors’ Filecoin addresses on the Filecoin blockchain.  Naturally, the latter is more compelling.

- Practicality | We are serious about making this tool a reality, so we will be assessing if the tool is suitable for practical uses, able to deploy and able to scale. This should be a product that can be deployed to mainnet without needing to rewrite and much adjustment/auditing. Please articulate clearly your design decisions and why it is suitable for the Filecoin Orbit program.

tracks.name: Scaling with InterPlanetary Consensus - Most meaningful deployment of a dApp on a newly launched custom subnet
tracks.description:
Create a custom purpose subnet using InterPlanetary Consensus (IPC) and a dApp that utilizes General Message Passing (GMP) between the subnet and its parent network.  This is early developer access to this technology.
## 🗂️ Bounty Category
  
Launch MVP on Testnet or Mainet
## 📚 Resources
  
https://ipc.space
https://docs.ipc.space
https://github.com/consensus-shipyard/ipc

  
https://youtu.be/rvLN_Us1x9o
## 🏆 Winner Breakdown
  
1st Place gets $5,000
## 📝 Requirements
  
With IPC, decentralized apps can reach planetary-scale through recursively scalable subnets, sub-second transactions, robust compute workloads, and highly adaptable WebAssembly runtimes tailored to dev requirements. It enables the creation of flexible, living networks of customizable sidechains or "subnets", which can achieve massive scaling by running parallel chains that interoperate with one another.
For this bounty, we are looking for projects that utilize our recently released General Message Passing (GMP) functionality that allows contracts on the parent and child subnets to communicate with each other. To qualify for this bounty, you will need to:
- Set up a subnet anchored to Calibration or Mycelium.
- Build any meaningful dApp on your subnet. 
- Utilize GMP to interact between the parent and child subnets for any cross-subnet features of your dApp. For example, bridging FT or NFT between subnets for DeFi solutions.
You can find out more about GMP at the IPC docs site at https://docs.ipc.space
Only projects that utilize GMP are eligible for this bounty.
## ✅ What does a successful project look like?
  
This is new functionality that we are just releasing for developers to get early access to. So there be dragons! But we are looking for developers to test it out and build projects that utilize GMP and call from the custom subnet to the parent network. Contracts on the parent network need to be made aware of IPC and expose an entrypoint for the subnet contract. The specifics of this are detailed in the IPC docs.
## 🎨 UI/UX Design Requirements
  
We are mainly interested in the smart contract side of things. If you have a UI/UX then that is a bonus, but we are mostly interested in your ideas and implementation of GMP.
## 🤝 Impact on our organization
  
Projects working on this bounty will give us valuable feedback on the process of deploying testnets and testing the recently developed GMP functionality.
## 🧑‍⚖️ How are we judging it?
  
The project needs to have smart contracts deployed to an IPC subnet. You will need to spin up your own custom L2 subnet anchored to the Filecoin testnet (called Calibration), or a L3 subnet anchored to the IPC L2 testnet (called Mycelium). Your smart contract will need to utilize GMP and make a call between your subnet and the parent network.
## 👀 Some example projects
  
Filecoin’s EVM (FEVM) allows you to access metadata about storage deals on the Filecoin network. But transacting on the main Filecoin L1 can be slow, as transactions take 60-90 seconds to execute. IPC subnets allow much faster (and cheaper) transactions, but don’t have access to the Filecoin storage deal data on L1. One example could be an NFT or DataDAO project running on an IPC subnet that uses GMP to access storage deal data on the parent (L1) network.
## 💰 Grant and Investment Opportunities
  
Details on the Filecoin Foundation developer grant program can be found here: https://grants.filecoin.io/

tracks.name: Scaling with InterPlanetary Consensus – Best Use of Custom Syscalls or Built-in Actors to extend the Filecoin Virtual Machine (FVM)
tracks.description:
Using IPC to allow you to deploy a custom subnet, develop some functionality that goes beyond what you can do natively with just Solidity. Use custom syscalls and Rust built-in actors in the Filecoin Virtual Machine (FVM) to achieve this.
## 🗂️ Bounty Category
  
Launch MVP on Testnet or Mainet
## 📚 Resources
  
https://ipc.space
https://docs.ipc.space
https://textile.notion.site/SQLite-FVM-Actor-Guide-e059bf438aea418ea430ad8d897482a1#adec333c3a7042f4b4027635833f4ac8

  
https://youtu.be/rvLN_Us1x9o
## 🏆 Winner Breakdown
  
1st Place gets $2,500
## 📝 Requirements
  
With IPC, decentralized apps can reach planetary-scale through recursively scalable subnets, sub-second transactions, robust compute workloads, and highly adaptable WebAssembly runtimes tailored to dev requirements. It enables the creation of flexible, living networks of customizable sidechains or "subnets", which can achieve massive scaling by running parallel chains that interoperate with one another.
For this bounty, we are looking for projects that customize the IPC subnets utilizing Pluggable syscalls or Custom built-in actors. To qualify for this bounty, you will need to:
1. Implement the extended features with either Pluggable syscalls or Custom built-in actors in Rust.
2. Deploy the customized subnet.
3. Demonstrate the customized subnet features with a demo or dApp.
You can find out more about these features in the IPC docs site: https://docs.ipc.space
Only projects that utilize one of the above features are eligible for this bounty.
## ✅ What does a successful project look like?
  
This is new functionality that we are just releasing for developers to get early access to. So there be dragons! The two new features allow you to customize the FVM (Filecoin Virtual Machine) in two specific new ways:
- Custom actors let you write on chain logic. They have the same limitations as any smart contract i.e they can't call program off-chain programs eg from the host machine. Their logic must be encapsulated within them.
- A pluggable syscall is a function set up and exposed to FVM for any contract to use. It allows actor to make external functions to the running node, the host machine etc. Examples:
- Prior to pluggable syscalls, FVM only had access to builtin syscalls eg to get the randomness from Lotus (which in turn gets it from Drand)
    - 
    - With pluggable syscalls, Fluence actors can interact with the RandomX which is a Proof of Work algorithm running on their nodes (off chain).
## 🎨 UI/UX Design Requirements
  
We are mainly interested in the smart contract side of things. If you have a UI/UX then that is a bonus, but we are mostly interested in your ideas and implementation of custom actors and/or pluggable syscalls.
## 🤝 Impact on our organization
  
Projects working on this bounty will give us valuable feedback on the process of deploying testnets and testing the recently developed pluggable syscalls and custom actor functionality.
## 🧑‍⚖️ How are we judging it?
  
The project needs to be deployed to an IPC subnet. You will need to spin up your own custom L2 subnet anchored to the Filecoin testnet (called Calibration), or a L3 subnet anchored to the IPC L2 testnet (called Mycelium). You will need to customise the build to include your new built-in actors (see Tableland example in the linked resources) and/or include your custom syscalls.
## 👀 Some example projects
  
The Filecoin EVM (FEVM) has all the general restrictions of any EVM and coding in Solidity. Hence trying to do something like parsing JSON data in Solidity is not practically possible. Utilizing a custom built-in actor you could embed or implement a simple JSON parser that is then callable from Solidity smart contracts.
EVM smart contacts run in a sandbox and don’t have access to outside resources. Utilizing a custom syscall, you could create a function that could return some outside information or data. E.g. fetch data from a local data store on the host. You would need to ensure it runs in a timely manner and deal with consensus of the data.
## 💰 Grant and Investment Opportunities
  
Details on the Filecoin Foundation developer grant program can be found here: https://grants.filecoin.io/

tracks.name: ZK is the Endgame
tracks.description:
Zero-knowledge continues to dominate Ethereum narratives and Polygon is at the forefront of these efforts. In this bounty, we are inviting builders to incorporate ZK in their projects in new and innovative ways. We have two ZK tracks for your consideration.

## 🗂️ Bounty Category
Onchain Security Bounty

## 📚 Resources
- [Understanding the zkEVM](https://docs.polygon.technology/zkEVM/overview/)
- [Circom Documentation](https://docs.circom.io/)
- [Polynomial Identity Language](https://docs.polygon.technology/zkEVM/spec/pil/)
- [zkASM](https://docs.polygon.technology/zkEVM/spec/zkasm/)

        
## 🏆 Winner Breakdown
We are selecting two winners
Team 1 gets $2500
Team 2 gets $2500
If there are not two top projects, we might only give out some of the prizes listed above, or we may adjust prize amounts. If no project is good enough to win, we'll explain why.

## 📝 Requirements
An innovative project that uses zero-knowledge to preserve user privacy or extend the use of existing zero-knowledge applications in blockchain, such as the zkEVM. This is an open bounty where we are looking for exciting ZK builders who want to build on top of Polygon using any ZK DSL of their choice.

## ✅ What does a successful project look like?
A clear demonstrable use of zero-knowledge primitives. You have to write your own circuits and demonstrate an innovative use of an existing ZK primitive or build one of your own. If you’re building a privacy app, then we would like to see you incorporate a minimally invasive user experience.

## 🎨 UI/UX Design Requirements
User experience lies at the heart of a successful ZK implementation, we are excited to see how you can build a delightful experience for your privacy apps or deliver a great performance improvement using ZK in a way that solves different problems.  You can build a Privacy App with an interface or have no UI at all.

## 🤝 Impact on our organization
We want to support ZK builders. Additionally, the zkEVM has multiple ways in which in builders can engage with the core technology and build cool extensions. The General ZK bounty doesn’t have impact but the zkEVM track extends the use of our protocol
     
## 🧑‍⚖️ How are we judging it?
You need to either write your own circuits or demonstrate skilled use of existing ZK primitives.  
Functional circuits are the main criteria. Circuits are code. You can use an ZK DSL to do this.

## 👀 Some example projects
General ZK Ideas:
- Privacy-Preserving Token Standards:
    - Define and implement privacy-preserving token standards for zkEVM chains. This involves creating a standard for issuing, transferring, and burning tokens while maintaining privacy through zero-knowledge proofs.
- Dual-Key Stealth Addresses:
    - Utilize dual-key stealth addresses to enhance privacy in the context of asset transfers. This involves generating unique one-time addresses for each transaction, making it difficult to trace the flow of assets on the blockchain.
- Blinded Signatures:
    - Use blinded signature schemes to allow for the signing of transactions on one chain without revealing the details to the signer. This can be particularly useful for multi-signature setups where multiple parties are involved in the validation process.

zkEVM Ideas:
- Homomorphic Encryption for State Transfers:
    - Explore the use of homomorphic encryption for securely transferring state information between zkEVM chains [CDK chains] through the bridge[LxLy]. This would allow the destination chain to perform computations on encrypted state data without decryption.
- zkEVM State Channels:
    - Design state channels that leverage the zkEVM to enable off-chain, private transactions between participants. This can reduce on-chain congestion and enhance scalability while maintaining privacy.

tracks.description:
Fhenix is an L2 on ETH that uses Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) to provide confidentiality. For our track, we are looking for developers who are interested in building full-stack applications in the Fhenix ecosystem that use encrypted computation. This can be anything from on-chain poker, dark pools, confidential voting, etc. We’re open to ideas and look forward to seeing what you and your team come up with!
## 🗂️ Bounty Category
  
Launch MVP on Testnet or Mainet
## 📚 Resources
  
Website: https://www.fhenix.io/ 
New Docs: https://fhenixprotocol.github.io/fhenix-docs/ 
Getting Started: https://www.fhenix.io/getting-started/ 
Cheat Sheet: https://www.fhenix.io/cheat-sheet/ 
Use Cases: https://www.fhenix.io/use-cases/ 
Discord Support: https://discord.gg/fhenix-io
Dev Rel Telegram @Corsola26

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=00XpLPxz7IY

## 🏆 Winner Breakdown
  
1st Place: $2500
2nd Place: $1500
3rd Place: $1000
## 📝 Requirements
  
We require a full stack application demonstration, live hosting is preferred but not mandatory. However, creating an application that others can play around with from their own machines would be beneficial for the team's prospects of being selected.

A Github repository with a history of commits is also required. In addition to a corresponding readme that makes it easy for developers, judges and our team to understand the overarching architecture of the project submission.

Finally teams must submit their official application before the deadline in order to qualify for prize considerations.
## ✅ What does a successful project look like?
  
A successful submission will follow all of the requirements. We are looking for projects that have the potential to contribute something new and creating to the Fhenix ecosystem. This means that we would ideally like to see full stack applications that are ready to be hosted on a public domain and use encrypted computation. These projects should bring something new to the ecosystem, not specifically the field. We would like to see projects successfully integrated as a usable product for our testnet, so that other community members have the opportunity to participate as well. Test cases will also better help us discern between successful and unsuccessful projects.

Aside from the product side of things, we would like to see collaborative and methodical increments to the underlying codebase. This means that teams should be pushing as often as is pragmatic for each dev. We don’t want to see a few single large pushes.
## 🎨 UI/UX Design Requirements
  
For UI/UX requirements, the simpler and easier to understand the better. Ideally we would like developers to begin to think about ways that state of the art account abstraction advancements can be integrated into their projects as well. The only major technical requirement is successful integration of the fhenix.js library into the client side of the application submission. Ideally we would like to see a clean styling (in terms of design principals) that are specifically tailored to the individual contracts and applications. It would be great to exemplify how much easier it is to create more advancement encrypted states using fhe vs zk.
## 🤝 Impact on our organization
  
We are looking for projects that we can feature in terms of our ecosystem growth. Potential for roll over bounties and grants are things that can be considered as well. Intertwining dev product submission into our larger ecosystem assets and point systems is something that we would like to explore.
## 🧑‍⚖️ How are we judging it?
  
We are looking for projects that are creative and technically complex. The ideal project would be a novel application of our FHE operations, that hasn’t been seen before. This can be in the form of novel library integrations, applications or even contract logic built. We are looking for robustness, as stated, we want to reward and promote projects that we believe will be contributing products in our ecosystem. Ideally we would like to see applications that show off the unique features that are idiosyncratic to Fhe specifically. We require that project are able to run on the Fhenix network as well use the necessary core libraries, in order to make sure our stack integration. Basically, why do you need composable privacy, vs traditional point of attestation privacy. Where can FHE fit in where zk falls short. We will be judging UX/UI primarily on the criteria of user flow regarding abi integration and the fhe-contract itself. We'd like to see ciphertext formation and permission management integrated seamlessly into the application, to mimic the usability of a traditional encrypted application, or as close as possible.

tracks.name: Best Use of Particle Network’s Modular Smart Wallet-as-a-Service on Mobile
tracks.description:
Implement Particle Network’s Smart Wallet-as-a-Service (AA-enabled social logins) within an existing or new consumer-facing mobile application. Particle Network enables Web2-like UX; thus, this bounty rewards the best mobile UX and implementation.
## 🗂️ Bounty Category
  
Launch MVP on Testnet or Mainet
## 📚 Resources
  
Documentation 
https://developers.particle.network
https://developers.particle.network/docs/android
https://developers.particle.network/docs/ios

GitHub Links
https://github.com/Particle-Network
https://github.com/Particle-Network/particle-ios
https://github.com/Particle-Network/particle-android
https://developers.particle.network/docs/example-repositories

Guides
https://developers.particle.network/docs/mobile-androidios-quickstart
https://developers.particle.network/reference/auth-android 
https://developers.particle.network/reference/auth-ios

How-to Videos
https://developers.particle.network/docs/tutorial-videos

  
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Hh7jp1VDw1c
## 🏆 Winner Breakdown
  
Given a distribution of 10,000 USDC to three winning projects,

1st place will receive $5,000

2nd place can get as much as $4,000 ($3,000 minimum)

3rd place can get as much as $2,000 ($1,000 minimum)

2nd and 3rd place will deviate in prize by $1,000 depending on quality; although the total will remain as 10,000 USDC. The quality of the 2nd and 3rd only impacts the distribution of the remaining $5,000 between the two.

The only situation in which the total prize amount, 10,000 USDC, would change is if there are less than three satisfactory submissions, in which total prize allocation would change accordingly.
## 📝 Requirements
  
This bounty aims to reward projects that effectively integrate Particle Network’s Modular Smart Wallet-as-a-Service within mobile applications to craft a consumer-ready experience, driven either in whole or in part by Particle Network’s tech stack. This application should either be an existing or new application (such as one already being built during ETHDenver) meant to interface with consumers in some capacity (the degree to which it’s consumer-facing is flexible). Within the application, users should have the option to onboard through social logins powered by either Particle Auth (direct library for facilitating social logins) or Particle Connect (Particle’s in-house connection kit). Onboarding should lead to a smart account, not an EOA –this can be facilitated through Particle’s AA SDK or an external AA SDK, with Particle Network acting as a Signer. The way in which this smart account is leveraged is up to the developer, although we suggest that it be used to further enhance the underlying UX of the application in question. Beyond these features (social logins and account abstraction driven by Particle Network), the specifics of your application (how it works, the vertical in which it exists, etc.) are up to you. Your application must be open-source.
## ✅ What does a successful project look like?
  
The most successful submissions to this bounty will have used Particle Network’s Smart Wallet-as-a-Service to enhance UX and craft a natural onboarding flow beyond the surface level. Specifically, this application should showcase the underlying technology and its implications for user experience; how it does this is up to the builder. One solid example of a successful implementation of Particle Network would be https://www.apex.exchange, in which users undergo a seamless onboarding process further enhanced by in-app UI elements built specifically to aid in making the integration of Particle feel more natural for end-users, resulting in a Web2-like experience. Although, as mentioned, the way in which your application achieves this natural onboarding flow is flexible –if your neighbor could onboard and use your application with minimal confusion, then you’ve likely hit the mark on this attribute.
## 🎨 UI/UX Design Requirements
  
Sign-in through social logins powered by Particle Network should be a visible and clear path of onboarding, resulting in an account that is handled naturally by the application. Beyond this, the types of UI elements used and the underlying UX flow are open-ended.
## 🤝 Impact on our organization
  
Particle Network seeks to highlight high-quality implementations of its technology within mobile applications, specifically to be used in examples and to raise awareness within the developer ecosystem. A well-thought-out, open-source mobile implementation of Particle Network’s SDKs can be enormously helpful in further showcasing this technology.
## 🧑‍⚖️ How are we judging it?
  
This bounty won’t be strict, and thus the judges will be applying open-minded criteria allowing projects to stretch across a variety of verticals and implementation methods. Judges will primarily focus on the dynamic between the onboarding process (with Particle Network) and the application itself, exploring the flow from login to usage. Beyond the UX of the application itself, judges will also take the associated open-source repository into account, exploring the programmatic implementation of Particle Network and the quality of its handling (referring back to how we define a quality/natural integration, but from a more technical lens).
## 👀 Some example projects
  
Web3 has historically been an almost exclusively engineering-focused financial sector. Just in the last few years have consumer applications grown to be a focus. Significant progress in this sector has been made over the past 12 months, specifically in furthering the adoption of ERC-4337 account abstraction for flexible, user-friendly account structures alongside Wallet-as-a-Service for familiar onboarding. As such, Web3 can finally make the transition to a consumer-focused sector with mass adoption soon. We hope to explore the potential in this regard through Modular Smart Wallet-as-a-Service, thus this bounty focuses on one of the most crucial fronts for consumer applications –mobile
## 💰 Grant and Investment Opportunities
  
Some winners with exceptional submissions may qualify for continued support from Particle Network through a grant, although this will be pursued at Particle Network’s discretion.
