tracks.name: Across: Web2 Cross-chain UX for Your Dapp!
tracks.description:
Harness our intents framework to give your dapp a reimagined cross-chain UX. Hack on Across V3 products to capitalize on our unparalleled cross-chain settlement layer or bundle bridge + dapp functions for abstracted bridging at the protocol level.
## 🗂️ Bounty Category
  
Feature Integration
## 📚 Resources
  
https://docs.across.to
https://github.com/across-protocol
https://discord.across.to
https://www.youtube.com/@acrossprotocol

  
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bPy09L9zA1E
## 🏆 Winner Breakdown
  
**First place:** $5,000
**Second place:** $2,000
**Third place:** $1,000 x3
## 📝 Requirements
  
Across is an interoperability protocol powered by intents. Our V3 upgrade has just went live and we are so excited to see what interesting cross-chain products you can build to push the boundaries of interoperability with us! We’re looking for creative ways of harnessing the power of intents with our suite of cross-chain features.

What we’re looking for:
- Integration of Across+ (bridge + action transaction bundles) into a dapp
- Building a UI that gives end users the opportunity to receive better pricing on bridge transfers via auction (similar to UniswapX, 1inch Fusion auction mechanisms, integrating the Across V3 cross-chain settlement system)
What we’re not looking for: 
- A dapp that simply adds the Across bridge API to its UI
## ✅ What does a successful project look like?
  
Our team is most inspired by elegant interoperability solutions, particularly moving away from message-passing as the prevailing solution to interoperability and instead enabling users to express and achieve their desired outcome while abstracting cross-chain execution to trustless 3rd parties -- intent based interoperability.

Across is built on an intents-based architecture composed of 3 levels:
1. An order flow auction layer to ingest users’ desired outcomes, often in the form of a cross-chain limit order
2. A network of 3rd parties (relayers) competing to fulfill that outcome with their own capital 
3. A system to escrow user funds, verify intent fulfillment, and repay those 3rd parties. We think this system simplifies interoperability into this two step process: 
    a. A user's assets are moved (or swapped) from X on chain A to Y on chain B + 
    b. A user's desired action is then executed on the destination chain. 

We are interested in features that make use of this architecture, powered by intents, to solve interoperability challenges. One example would be to harness this framework to deploy your dapp on one chain and pull capital from any chain, rather than deploying your dapp on multiple chains to access siloed capital. It's an elegant solution that not only benefits developers by saving precious engineering resources, but one that you can use to attract users since it removes the tediousness of the bridging process from their to-do list. You can also takes things a step further by improving any layer of the Across system, such as designing a robust order flow auction to truly enable cross-chain limit orders (which Across doesn't _yet_ offer)
## 🎨 UI/UX Design Requirements
  
For UI/UX, web-based or CLI-based UI will be accepted. If someone can show something on a CLI then it should be achievable to port it to a web interface. 

Projects will not be judged more favorably for including flashy web interfaces. (Don't worry about spending too much time on this!)
## 🤝 Impact on our organization
  
It provides validation of our V3 protocol upgrade, gives our project a more robust ideas bank, and garners insights on the perception of our upgrade and its respective developer tools.
## 🧑‍⚖️ How are we judging it?
  
We are evaluating this bounty based on the depth of integration with Across v3 products and the creativity of use cases. To clarify, "deep" integration involves comprehensive utilization of Across v3's capabilities, such as incorporating features, functionalities, and seamless interaction within the Across ecosystem. Regarding the use cases we're seeking to solve, participants should consider the examples provided, such as leveraging Across+ Ideas Bank for Bridge + Action Bundling scenarios, including Bridge + LP, Bridge + Borrow/Lend, Bridge + Swap, Bridge + Receive destination gas token with transfer, and Bridge + Bet. Additionally, novel cross-chain order flow auction designs for the Cross-Chain Settlement System are encouraged. We're looking for innovative solutions that demonstrate creativity, potential market impact, improvement in user experience, and technical complexity. Participants are reminded that hacks may be submitted on testnets (e.g., Sepolia), mainnet, or on a local network, as long as the new functionalities are clearly demonstrated.
## 👀 Some example projects
  
Please note that hacks may be submitted on testnets (e.g., Sepolia), mainnet, or on a local network, as long as the new functionalities are clearly demonstrated.

**Across+ Ideas Bank (Bridge + Action Bundling aka Cross-chain bridge hooks) :**
1. Bridge + LP - Siphon capital from any chain and into a staking contract on your dapp. Bundled transaction example: Bridge 1 ETH from Mainnet to Optimism, swap 0.5 ETH to 1000 USDC on Optimism, deposit 0.5 ETH and 1000 USDC into Uniswap WETH/USDC pool.
2. Bridge + Borrow/Lend - Pull capital from any chain and enter into a lending or borrowing position. Bundled transaction example: Bridge 1 ETH from Mainnet to Arbitrum (e.g) and add supply into Aave’s ETH market, sending resulting aTokens to user’s EOA on Arbitrum.
3. Bridge + Swap - Pull funds from the user’s home chain to complete a bid on an NFT on your dapp’s chain. Bundled transaction example: Bridge 0.5 ETH from Mainnet to Arbitrum (e.g), swap for 1,100 $MAGIC tokens, send 1,100 $MAGIC to NFT seller’s EOA
4. Bridge + Receive destination gas token with transfer. Bundled transaction example: Bridge an ERC-20 and swap a portion of it on the destination chain into the destination chain’s native gas token.
5. Bridge + Bet - Encourage protocol activity by removing the bridging hurdle and place a bet on Polymarket (e.g) from any chain. Bundled transaction example: Bridge token to destination chain and place bet on open Polymarket predictions.

**Cross-Chain Settlement System Ideas Bank:**
Novel cross-chain order flow auction designs - The first layer in the intent architecture is an order flow auction. Design an OFA (order flow auction) that allows a user to specify a cross-chain limit order (swap X on chain A to Y on chain B for some minimum amount, by some deadline) for a network of 3rd parties (relayers) to compete in to offer the best price _and _speed.

# What Will The Internet Look Like For ETHDenver 2024
The IT team for ETHDenver 2024 has performed a comprehensive assessment of the state of the IT infrastructure for the upcoming show, this included 2 site visits, review of internal communications about issues, and collection of explicit feedback from stakeholders. During this assessment the IT team identified the following major pain points and have taken steps to remediate:
• Undersized core infrastructure which likely resulted in dropped connections when the firewall state table filled up
• Undersized NAT Pool causing throttling to various services due to an uneven distribution of connections
• Lack of access point density in the BUIDLHub resulting in dropped connections and overloaded equipment

Throughout the venue the IT team is taking steps to identify wireless dead zones and improve coverage proactively, they have developed reactionary plans to resolve reported dead zones in real time, during the event through tactical deployment of equipment. No more than 20-25 clients per access point. After careful consideration, they have decided to deploy network switches at each row to provide optional hardwired connectivity.
